title: Wendell and the Provision
premise: Ada Dunmore has spent seven years running salvage digs across the Bay of Bengal, keeping one rule: never work the Sundarbans concession her father died surveying. When her father's old rival, Marguerite Hale, buys out Ada's crew's debts and forces them onto that exact job—recovering a sealed archive before the colonial-era permits expire—Ada must choose between abandoning her found family and facing the river that took everything. Trapped by an early monsoon with a leaking boat, a forged permit, and Hale's hired enforcer closing in, Ada allies with Idris Rahman, a river pilot whose brother was jailed on evidence from her father's last expedition. Together they uncover that her father didn't die by accident—he was murdered to bury proof that the concession itself was built on stolen land—and Ada must decide whether justice means exposing it through channels that will destroy her crew, or burning the archive and letting the river keep its secret. She chooses exposure, at the cost of the permits, the boat, and nearly her life; in the aftermath she stops measuring life in miles and finally claims a place, and a person, to stay for.
about_author: Oscar Voss is the pen name of a former merchant marine cartographer who spent a decade charting delta waterways before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who find belonging in the places maps get wrong.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In Chittagong harbor, Ada finishes a routine salvage contract and plans the crew's next jump before anyone can ask her to stay. A debt collector delivers papers showing their boat mortgaged to Marguerite Hale. The beat is restless independence curdling into dread—the past arriving with paperwork.

chapters.title: The Rival's Terms
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hale offers a clean slate if the crew recovers a sealed survey archive from the Sundarbans station before the concession permits lapse in six weeks. Ada refuses; the crew, drowning in debt, votes without her. The beat is betrayal—her family choosing survival over her one sacred rule.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Helm
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The only pilot willing to run the delta in pre-monsoon season is Idris Rahman, who recognizes Ada's surname and says nothing. He takes the job for reasons of his own: his brother's case file cites her father's expedition. The beat is wary mutual use masking old wounds.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. First days upriver: drowned villages, half-sunk markers, and Ada realizing the delta has changed since her childhood here. Idris saves her from a collapsing channel and lets slip he knew her father. The beat is grief surfacing in unfamiliar water.

chapters.title: The Station
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. They reach the abandoned survey station and find it stripped—but not looted: someone official removed records recently. Ada finds her father's hidden field notes describing a land seizure disguised as a concession. The beat is discovery sharpening into suspicion that his death was no accident.

chapters.title: Hale's Man
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hale's enforcer Vasquez arrives with a second boat and orders: recover the archive, leave nothing else standing—including witnesses. A night skirmish holes the hull below the waterline. The beat is fear made physical; the job turns from salvage to survival.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The early monsoon traps them in a mangrove channel with a leaking boat and Vasquez hunting by radio. Bailing water side by side, Ada and Idris trade truths: her father's guilt over his testimony, his brother's wrongful conviction. The beat is intimacy forged under threat—love beginning against both their duties.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following her father's notes to a raised cache, they open the archive: full documentation that the concession sits on forcibly taken land, plus a letter naming Hale's firm as complicit in the cover-up—and implying her father was silenced. The beat is devastating clarity: the truth is worth more than the permits, and worth less than their lives to the wrong people.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Climax. With hours left on the permits, Vasquez corners them at the confluence; Ada scuttles her own boat to strand his, and the crew mutinies against Hale mid-confrontation. Idris takes a bullet shielding the archive; Ada chooses not to burn it but to carry it out. The beat is sacrifice and refusal—justice claimed outside any law that would bury it.

chapters.title: Where the Maps Get Wrong
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Resolution. The archive reaches a journalist and a land-rights court; Hale's concessions collapse, Idris's brother walks free, and the crew keeps a smaller, honest boat. Ada, who once planned her escape before the ropes were tied, unpacks her bags in a house above the pilot station. The beat is arrival—belonging chosen, love stayed for, miles finally measured in years.
